title: Google's third Gemini Flash in six weeks — this one defenders-only
summary: Google shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash plus a restricted Flash Cyber variant for vetted defenders, with outside patching numbers from Chrome and Wiz — and a curl case the same week where two frontier security tools found nothing and a specialist filed 29 reports. Plus TimesFM-3's cross-series attention, and a report tracing 215,128 machine-generated 'best software' pages that Perplexity cites.

topics: Gemini 3.8 Flash and the restricted 3.8 Flash Cyber variant: capability gating by access program, Google's claim that cybersecurity training drove general software-engineering gains, CWE-Bench 47.2% pass@1 against 47.8% for the leading frontier model, >70% vulnerability-discovery success across 20 languages, Chrome's 2.6x correct-patch figure and Wiz's recall-per-cost figure, and the curl counter-case where Mythos and Codex security returned nothing and AISLE's 29 reports yielded 6 low-severity CVEs

TimesFM-3: alternating causal temporal attention and full variate attention over a series-by-time grid, 32-step patches, lookahead tokens for known-future covariates, non-autoregressive contiguous patch masking emitting 9 quantiles across the whole horizon, 330M parameters on a trillion-point corpus

Trellner Research's citation audit of Perplexity: 7,534 citations across 2,055 domains, 59.8% outside the top 100k sites, and three co-registered domains publishing 215,128 templated 'best software' pages addressed to retrievers rather than readers

threads.name: Frontier-model release gating
threads.status: Google joined the pattern with Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, a separate model name restricted to vetted defenders through an application program while the general Flash model ships to anyone at 75 cents per million input tokens — and Google credits cybersecurity training for the general model's software-engineering gains, so part of the gated capability is arguably already on general sale.
threads.arc: From a release/no-release decision, to a graded product line with a published score per configuration, to a third lab in four days shipping the restricted tier as its own model behind an access form — with the hosts unresolved on whether the form is a wall or only a tilt.

threads.name: AI vulnerability discovery versus real codebases
threads.status: Daniel Stenberg reported on August 24 that Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's Codex security tooling found nothing further in curl; AISLE's autonomous system then filed 29 reports, 6 of which curl validated as low-severity CVEs in 8.22.0, and curl's pending CVE count went from 3 to 10 within four days.
threads.arc: Opens as the first public side-by-side of frontier-lab security tooling against a specialist system on the most-audited small codebase in wide deployment, and surfaces precision — 23 of 29 reports were not vulnerabilities — as the metric no model card publishes.

dives.story: Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, the access-gated cyber variant, against the curl result
dives.why_it_matters: Security teams deciding whether to apply for a gated defender model need to know that benchmark recall on already-discovered vulnerabilities says little about discovery in a hardened codebase, and that maintainer-facing precision — 23 false reports for every 6 real ones — is the cost nobody publishes.

dives.story: TimesFM-3's cross-series attention and single-pass quantile forecasting
dives.why_it_matters: Forecasting, inventory and capacity teams get a 330M-parameter zero-shot model that handles covariates and emits nine quantiles per horizon step, which makes 'try the foundation model first' an afternoon rather than a project — though whether it beats a tuned in-house model on your own data is unanswered.

dives.story: Trellner's citation audit and the 215,128 pages manufactured for retrieval
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone relying on an AI answer engine for product or vendor selection is exposed to a supply side that builds pages addressed to retrievers, in a pipeline with no popularity prior and no provenance check — and reading the citation list is the available defense.

concepts_taught: alternating causal-temporal and full-variate attention over a series-by-time grid: attention along the row learns temporal pattern, attention down the column learns cross-series relationships without hand-specifying which variables interact

non-autoregressive quantile forecasting: contiguous patch masking emits the whole horizon in one forward pass, predicting nine quantiles per step, so the decision variable is a percentile rather than a mean

why benchmark recall on vulnerability datasets overstates in-the-wild discovery: benchmarks are built from bugs somebody already found, while what remains in a hardened codebase is by construction the set that survived prior searching — and precision, not recall, is what costs a maintainer
